source.method: Manual review of the full public video using watch skill frames and native TikTok captions
source.pacing_basis: 242 caption words / 76.281 seconds; approximately 190 words per minute
source.limitations: Native captions stop before the final 11.5 seconds; final beat is described from frames. No retention analytics or causal performance data were available. The original creator character prompt is unavailable; FRAME character blocks are analyst-observed. Music, sound effects, and continuous camera travel were not assessed from sampled frames and captions.

hook_analysis.verbal_hook: In 1981, a teenage boy visits a worn down arcade in his hometown of Portland, Oregon.
hook_analysis.visual_hook_description: A dark exterior of Furby's Arcade with MISSING posters already visible on the storefront and mailbox; the story's apparent consequence is planted before the boy enters.
hook_analysis.retention_trigger: The unexplained missing-person posters and an unmarked arcade cabinet suggest that the ordinary arcade conceals a threat.

narrative_beats.summary: Places a teenage boy at a Portland arcade in 1981. Missing posters appear in the exterior shot before the narrator calls attention to them.
The boy notices the black Polybius cabinet, which lacks a maker, serial number, and service details. The owner dismisses his question.
Playing the game brings euphoria. He returns daily, while surreal orange duplicates and missing time show its grip on him.
He pulls away, finds missing-person posters bearing his own face, and discovers the exits are locked. A control monitor hints at a recognition and erasure test.
narrative_beats.on_screen_text: SELF-RECOGNITION TEST IN PROGRESS; ERASURE FAILURE!

narrative_beats.summary: He forces open a staff door and finds a dark room of identical Polybius cabinets. While running through them, he knocks one down.
He lies on the floor; another figure is visible in the shadows. A suited man emerges from a bright server room with a glowing device. The video ends before explaining the device or the boy's fate.

pattern_interrupts: Around 0:25, the ordinary arcade gives way to surreal floating orange duplicates.
Around 0:51, missing posters reveal the boy's face.
Around 1:00, the setting shifts behind a STAFF ONLY door into a room of identical cabinets.
Around 1:22, a brightly lit server room contrasts with the dark arcade as a suited man appears.

takeaways_for_remixing: Plant a consequence in the opening background, then make the protagonist discover its personal meaning later.
Introduce one concrete, anomalous object early; add a new clue or visual state as the character interacts with it.
Use a mid-story self-recognition turn to convert general danger into danger aimed at the protagonist.
If ending on a cliffhanger, make the final image pose a specific unresolved question. Test completion and rewatches before assuming that ambiguity helps reach.

frame_analysis.figure: No living person is identifiable in the sampled storefront views. Dark missing-person silhouettes appear on posters; the narrated boy is not yet visible in these sampled frames.
frame_analysis.room: Furby's Arcade exterior: green-and-white striped awning, pink neon sign, benches, street furniture, a parked red car, and several MISSING posters. Overcast daylight gives the street flat, cool light; the 1981 date comes from narration.
frame_analysis.action: The storefront is introduced with missing posters already in view before their significance is explained. This is a quick eight-second setup.
frame_analysis.movement: Vertical, street-level wide views of the facade. The sampled viewpoint shifts across the frontage; a continuous pan or dolly cannot be confirmed from extracted frames.
frame_analysis.extras:
Sound: Music and sound effects were not assessed from the frame-and-caption extraction.
Speech: Native captions place the story in Portland, Oregon, in 1981 and introduce a teenage visitor; no character dialogue is captioned.
Style: Stylized 3D exterior, pink neon against a gray sky, planted MISSING imagery, and bold yellow subtitles.
frame_analysis.dont_line: Keep the posters visible but unexplained at the opening; do not present the narrated urban-legend setup as verified history.

frame_analysis.action: The boy moves from the ordinary game aisle toward the unmarked black Polybius cabinet; its marquee becomes the focus. The reveal takes about ten seconds.
frame_analysis.movement: Low-to-medium-wide vertical framing places the cabinet left and boy right, then uses closer cabinet views. No continuous camera travel is verifiable from sampled frames.
frame_analysis.extras:

frame_analysis.room: The same arcade gives way to a more abstract presentation: central black cabinet, stretched multicolor floor, bright white overhead strips, and deep perspective. The visualized space has no reliable time-of-day cue.
frame_analysis.action: Starting the game shifts the boy from an ordinary standing player into a euphoric, disorienting visual state. The change is abrupt within roughly ten seconds.
frame_analysis.movement: A frontal wide view of the cabinet gives way to much broader, symmetrical views with floating figures at different depths. Cuts are visible in the sampled sequence; a continuous camera move is unverified.

frame_analysis.dont_line: Treat the floating duplicates as a visual expression of his experience, not as proven separate characters in the arcade.

frame_analysis.figure: The orange boy stands between Polybius and the arcade counter, turning away from the cabinet. A pale mannequin-like figure is visible near the counter in a sampled view.

frame_analysis.action: The boy pries himself away from the machine and puts distance between himself and it. The short beat slows into a moment of resistance.
frame_analysis.movement: Rear three-quarter medium-wide view keeps Polybius at frame left and the counter behind the boy. Camera travel is not established in sampled frames.

Style: His bright orange shape remains the focal point against the dark carpet and neon; yellow narration subtitles continue.
frame_analysis.dont_line: Keep the break from the game difficult and deliberate; do not add a new external rescuer or spoken warning.

frame_analysis.figure: A MISSING poster displays a human headshot that the narration identifies as the boy. A pale, faceless mannequin-like figure stands beside a nearby game in the sampled insert.
frame_analysis.room: Arcade wall and counter area with multiple MISSING posters, a bowling game, colorful floor, and low fluorescent/cabinet illumination. Indoor time of day remains indeterminate.
frame_analysis.action: The formerly anonymous poster becomes a reveal about the protagonist: the missing person's face is his. The clue lands quickly, over about six seconds.
frame_analysis.movement: Tighter poster insert replaces wider arcade coverage. The sampled stills do not support a specific pan, zoom, or track.
frame_analysis.extras:
Sound: Music and sound effects were not assessed from the frame-and-caption extraction.
Speech: Native captions say the posters throughout the arcade depict him.
Style: MISSING / HAVE YOU SEEN ME? print, pale faceless display figure, dim arcade color, and yellow subtitles sharpen the self-recognition reveal.
frame_analysis.dont_line: Let the poster reveal remain the discovery; avoid showing a different named missing person as the answer.
